propositions: Mutation test shards have stale historical survivor counts (814 vs 491 mutants in signing.py) that block unrelated work and cannot safely gate current code without evidence gathering and per-shard promotion.

The gate must distinguish three enforcement modes (advisory, ratchet, strict) with explicit per-shard configuration in .github/mutation-shards.toml, no duplicate repository-level mutmut config, and pinned timeout values (timeout_constant=1.0, timeout_multiplier=15.0).

Fresh isolated base/head archives with no persisted verdict cache must be used for evaluation, with per-shard 30-minute job limits, max-children=1 concurrency, clean-test preflight, and selector-derived matrix jobs.

Ratchet mode must preserve unchanged legacy survivors and no-tests outcomes, block killed regressions and new survivors, and accept only individually reviewed equivalent fingerprints for changed functions.
Strict mode must require every mutant to be killed or individually fingerprinted as equivalent, blocking all no-tests, timeouts, incomplete statuses, and zero-mutant runs.
